captions.instagram:
How does a radio work?

A radio pulls one voice out of an invisible sea of waves, using a coil, a capacitor and a diode. Open up a 1970s transistor set, shake charges into radio waves, play with AM and FM, tune a circuit into resonance and follow a signal through a superhet.

→ The household transistor radio: a ferrite rod, a tuning capacitor, a few transistors and a speaker.
→ Turn the knob and the capacitor plates slide together, tuning in a different station.
→ A radio wave is electric and magnetic fields rippling out at the speed of light.
→ By day the D layer swallows medium waves; at night they bounce off the sky, far away.
→ AM: the voice changes the size of the carrier wave. Static shows up as crackle.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/radioclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a radio work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A radio pulls one voice out of an invisible sea of waves, using a coil, a capacitor and a diode. Open up a 1970s transistor set, shake charges into radio waves, play with AM and FM, tune a circuit into resonance and follow a signal through a superhet.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/radioclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/radioclear

In this video:
• A few parts, no computer. A classic transistor radio is a ferrite rod antenna, a gang tuning capacitor, IF transformer cans, six or seven transistors, a detector diode, a speaker and four D cells (6 V).
• Waves of electric and magnetic field. Charges surging up and down an antenna send out linked electric and magnetic ripples at 300,000 km/s.
• A voice rides a carrier. AM changes the carrier's size, so its envelope traces the sound and it fits in a 9 kHz channel.
• Tuning is resonance. A coil and a capacitor ring at f = 1 / (2π√LC).
• The superheterodyne. A local oscillator runs 455 kHz above the station (10.7 MHz for FM).
• Radio in India. Akashvani reaches about 99% of Indians in 23 languages.
